# Den Leader Resources

The Den Meeting is the most important part of Cub Scouting.  It is where Cub
Scouts build friendships, work together to learn new things, and progress
towards earning their common badge of rank.  Serving as a Den Leader is
providing an opportunity to make a positive life long impact on your child and
others in the den.

## Conducting a Den Meeting

Den meetings are conducted at a date, time, and location that is best for
families that are in the den.  How often and for how long a den meets is also
up to each den.  The den should meet as frequently as necessary to ensure
that, at minimum, each Cub Scout in the den has the opportunity to earn their
badge of rank.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/BSA_0357-edit-photo-
CSBC-1.jpg)

## Preparing for a Den Meeting

Before you conduct a den meeting, complete the online training for Den Leader
found at **[my.scouting.org](https://my.scouting.org/)**.

To prepare for a den meeting simply identify a Cub Scout Adventure that you
want to complete.  Adventures are found in each of the grade-specific
handbooks.  It is recommended that you focus on the required Adventures first.

If this is your first den meeting for the year with new and returning Cub
Scouts, the Bobcat Adventure is designed to be done as your first required
Adventure.

Once you have chosen the Adventure to work on for your den meeting review the
webpage for that Adventure.  You can get to it by scanning the QR code in the
Cub Scout handbook or by following the links below.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/09/ptc-2-1024x681.jpg)![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/09/ptc-2-1024x681.jpg)

## Parts of a Den Meeting

There are three parts to a den meeting.  Before the meeting, during the
meeting, and after the meeting

### Before the Meeting

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-541.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Identify which Cub Scout Adventure you want to work on.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-542.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Review the webpage for the Adventure which includes the Safety Moment, the
Safety Moment highlights the key items you need to know to conduct the
Adventure safely, the requirements for the Adventure, and recommended
activities to complete each requirement.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-543.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Identify the activities you will do during your den meeting.  Gather the
necessary supplies and complete the “Before the Meeting” action items.

### During the Meeting

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-541.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Opening** – Conduct an opening ceremony that includes the pledge of
allegiance, the Scout Oath, and Scout Law.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-542.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Activities** – Complete the activities you chose to complete the
requirements for the Adventure.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-543.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Recognition** – If the requirements for an Adventure are completed,
recognize each Cub Scout with the Adventure Loop or Pin as instant
recognition.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-544.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Closing** – Conduct a formal closing using the living circle, make any
announcements or reminders, and the den leader may close with a reflection
that focuses on a value of the Scout Oath or Scout Law.

### After the Meeting

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-541.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Review** – The den leader, assistant den leader, and other adults who helped
with the meeting review how the meeting went and take any notes for
improvement for the next meeting.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-542.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Thank You** – The den leader sends thank you notes to those adults who
helped with the meeting.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/Frame-543.svg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%2098%2098%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Record** – The den leader records the requirement that were completed at the
meeting in **[Scoutbook](https://www.scouting.org/resources/scoutbook/)**.

Central.  Hosted by **Scouting** magazine this weekly show features the
National Director of Cub Scouting and/or the National Chair of Cub Scouting
addressing Cub Scout program questions.

All episodes are recorded and can be watched on the **Scouting** magazine
Facebook page. [**Cub Chat
